ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list (implemented via the United Nations Act), the Canadian schedule under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Criminal Code s 83.05 terrorist entity list, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list where USD payment rails are used. Politically exposed persons (foreign and domestic PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates) must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance. BC's Money Laundering Control Act (SBC 2022, c 27) imposes further reporting duties for suspicious transactions to the BC Civil Forfeiture Office and requires beneficial-ownership attestations. Negative-media and adverse-information verification via a commercial screening database is required before incorporation documents are filed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: OneStop Business Registry / BC Registry Services (Corporate Online) - https://www.onestop.ca and https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC company name must be expressed in English or French characters (Latin alphabet). The legal name may include a Latin-alphabet transliteration of a foreign script (e.g., Pinyin rendering of a Chinese hotpot brand) provided the transliteration is reasonably pronounceable in English or French. The registered legal name must appear in the Latin alphabet; Chinese characters may be used as a trade-style or business name only and must not be registered as the sole legal name. The name must contain a distinct element, a descriptive element, and must conclude with the corporate designator 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or 'S.R.I.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: British Columbia or BC (requires provincial consent)
any word implying government affiliation or royal patronage
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 56 calendar days and may be renewed by filing a further reservation before expiry. On rejection, the applicant should file a revised name through the OneStop portal. A formal reconsideration request may be submitted in writing to the Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9W1) within the reservation period, attaching the rejection notice, a NUANS search report, and a legal argument on distinctiveness and compliance with the BC Business Corporations Act Name Regulation, B.C. Reg. 224/2004. There is no statutory right to a tribunal hearing; the practical remedy is administrative re-submission or judicial review by the Supreme Court of British Columbia if the refusal is arbitrary or unreasonable. For restricted tokens, prior written consent of the relevant minister or regulator (e.g., Financial Institutions Commission for 'financial') is required before filing the incorporation documents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the statutory registered office: BCA s 194 requires a registered office in BC open to accept service of process during normal business hours, which may be satisfied by a licensed corporate services provider's physical address; a post-office box is prohibited. A virtual office is acceptable for the registered office and records office, but cannot substitute for the operational site of the hotpot restaurant. The restaurant itself must occupy a physical premises satisfying Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) food-establishment licensing, City of Vancouver zoning and business-licence requirements, fire and building code compliance, and WorkSafeBC registration. Commercial substance for a full-service dining chain requires a functional kitchen, dining area, condiment and sauce preparation area, cold-storage capacity, and local employment records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Vancouver Coastal Health unannounced food-safety inspections: greater than 95% probability within the first 90 days of operation, with recurring inspections thereafter. City of Vancouver business-licence compliance visits and zoning inspections: approximately 40%. WorkSafeBC health-and-safety inspections: approximately 30% around the opening period or after a workplace incident. Direct physical inspection of the registered office by the BC Registrar of Companies: approximately 5%; overall pre-incorporation registered-office site-visit risk is quantified at LOW (below 10%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), as amended, and B.C. Reg. 58/2004; key provisions: s. 10 (Articles), s. 11 (Notice of Articles), s. 27 (Incorporation Application), ss. 51-54 (Unlimited Liability Company structure, special shares and member liability), s. 124 (director residency), s. 130 (consent to act as director) and s. 190 (share issuance consideration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Mobile Services — British Columbia Corporate Registry (Ministry of Finance), Victoria, BC; filings submitted via the Corporate Online electronic platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Combined Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles (BC Corporate Registry Form 1 and Form 2, respectively) together with the ULC-specific Articles of Incorporation naming the corporation as an 'Unlimited Liability Company'; the filing is subject to the CAD 350.00 statutory fee (approx. USD 260).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a BC Unlimited Liability Company and no escrow-account deposit requirement at incorporation; shares may be issued for nominal consideration provided the consideration is not a discount to real value (BCBCA s. 190). The ULC must maintain at least one director ordinarily resident in Canada (BCBCA s. 124(2)).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This First Board Resolution, adopted by the sole incorporator and ratified by the initial directors immediately after incorporation, resolves as follows: (i) the corporation subscribes to the shares set forth in the Notice of Articles, namely Special Shares, Common Shares, and ULC Parallel Shares, with the authorized capital structure recorded in the Articles; (ii) the registered and records office of the corporation is established at the address stated in the Notice of Articles; (iii) the following individuals are appointed as directors, namely: ____; and (iv) the following officers are appointed, namely: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until their successors are duly elected or appointed. The President is further authorized to execute and deliver all ancillary banking, licensing, and regulatory documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Mobile Services — Corporate Online name-reservation queue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-mandated pre-screen and file a Name Reservation Request through Corporate Online, selecting a distinctive name that ends with 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. Attach the name-search report evidencing no confusingly similar existing BC corporate name.
required_dossiers: Signed statement of intent to reserve name (where requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under BCBCA s. 24, submit a written reconsideration request to the Registry providing trade-mark registrations or common-law use evidence; alternatively, reserve up to three alternative names on the same application to preserve the filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles, Notice of Articles and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (pre-filing review) / corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles with two or more classes of shares providing for Special Shares, Common Shares and ULC Parallel Shares, together with the Notice of Articles (Form 2) that sets out the registered office and record office, the first directors' names, and the authorized share structure. Each proposed director must sign a Consent to Act as Director (Form 9) acknowledging duties under BCBCA ss. 124 and 130.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director — Form 9
Registered Office and Records Office Address forms (Forms 5/6)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the pre-filing examiner issues a requisition addressing defective share-class provisions or missing mandatory agreements, file an amended Notice of Articles and revise the Articles; the Registry will re-review without imposing a new statutory filing fee on the corrected documents if submitted within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online (self-service portal) or an authorized BC Registry Partner Service Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online, upload the completed Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles together with the Articles and director consents, pay the statutory filing fee using a valid credit card or BC Registries account, and submit the package for statutory review. Confirm automatic receipt of the Payment Transaction Summary and application tracking number.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director — Form 9
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete fields or inconsistent share data, use the Corporate Online 'Continue Application' function to correct and resubmit within 30 days without an additional fee; if the rejection alleges non-compliance with BCBCA s. 27, obtain legal certification and file a fresh application with the Certification of Compliance attaching a legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (Certificate issuance) and corporate registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation from Corporate Online and hold an organizational meeting of the board within one month. At the meeting adopt the corporate seal policy (if any), approve a banking resolution, issue share certificates against the subscribed share consideration, appoint officers, and approve standard by-laws for ULC governance.
required_dossiers: Directors' and shareholders' minutes for organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains typographical errors, file a 'Correction of Records' application under BCBCA s. 88 with a supporting affidavit; the Registry will issue a corrected certificate. If the banking institution refuses to open an account due to ULC unlimited-liability status, provide the bank with a certified copy of the Notice of Articles and Canadian-resident director evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Payroll, WorkSafeBC and Municipal Licensing Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance — Provincial Tax Office; WorkSafeBC; municipal Business Licence and permitting office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA for a Business Number and each required program account (Corporate Tax, GST/HST, Payroll), register with the BC Ministry of Finance for Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and employer health tax, obtain WorkSafeBC coverage for F&B operations, and file the municipal Business Licence application together with the Food Service Establishment permit request from the local health authority.
required_dossiers: CRA Request for a Business Number (RC1) with program-account schedule
BC PST registration and employer health tax forms
WorkSafeBC account application (Form 6 or 7 for food services)
Municipal business-licence application and health-permit plan review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or the BC Finance registry flags the ULC's exempt-pass-through status, submit a formal written objection with the Certificate of Incorporation and letter of tax clearance; if WorkSafeBC classifies the business in the wrong industry rate, exercise the Classification Review Request within 30 days of the notice and provide payroll and job-duty evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Department (e.g., City of Vancouver License Office) acting jointly with the Regional Health Authority (e.g., Vancouver Coastal Health Environmental Health Division) and BC Gas Safety authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Establishment Operating Permit under the Food Premises Regulation (Public Health Act, SBC 2008, c. 28), combined with a municipal Business Licence, catering/restaurant class 'Food Primary / Full-Service Dining'

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Assessment Office), with municipal drainage and Metro Vancouver regulation under the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District by-laws
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt tier for a sit-down hotpot restaurant; no full Environmental Assessment Certificate required under the Environmental Assessment Act (SBC 2018, c. 51). Site-specific waste-discharge registration and municipal sewer connection approval are mandatory before opening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: fats, oils and grease (FOG) in kitchen effluent must be reduced to <100 mg/L via an approved grease interceptor before discharge to the municipal sewer, per Metro Vancouver Sewer Use Bylaw; cooking-exhaust discharge must comply with the BC Mechanical Code and local smoke-odour nuisance thresholds; VOCs from seasoning preparation are below BC OGV AQMS reporting limits, and used cooking oil and solid food waste must be handled by a licensed transporter with documented diversion manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire department under the BC Fire Code for commercial cooking areas, Type I hood and automatic fire-suppression systems; structural load inspection of the floor slab for hotpot tables, refrigeration banks and ventilation supports; WorkSafeBC occupational clearance covering commercial kitchen safety, gas appliance installation permit, exhaust-hood cleaning schedule, and first-aid readiness prior to issuing the Certificate of Occupancy.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank; Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration. Sanctions administration is vested in the Department of Finance Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; OSFI supervises federally regulated banks; FINTRAC enforces AML/CFT obligations on financial intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is an IMF Article VIII freely convertible currency. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully liberalized; no exchange-control approvals or central-bank consents are required for inbound foreign direct investment into a British Columbia ULC or for outbound profit and dividend remittances. The only material remittance hurdles are tax-driven: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends and certain payments, deemed-dividend treatment on paid-up capital reductions under section 84 of the Income Tax Act, and treaty-reduced rates available under the Canada-United States Tax Convention.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender on export proceeds: there are no mandatory conversion timelines, no minimum conversion ratios, and no obligation to repatriate foreign currency earnings. Export receipts from condiment supply and franchise royalty streams may be retained offshore or in domestic foreign-currency accounts, subject only to FINTRAC large-transaction threshold reporting (CAD 10,000 or equivalent) and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account / Merchant Acquiring Settlement Account
Operating Account / Trade Finance (LC and Collections)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Auxiliary-only. Offshore digital EMIs are not viable as the sole or primary banking rail: they cannot clear CAD through Payments Canada, cannot accept deposits in Canada unless authorized as deposit-taking institutions, and must comply with the Bank of Canada-administered Retail Payment Activities Act registration regime introduced in 2024. Foreign EMIs (e.g., Wise payouts) are suitable only for low-value vendor disbursements; capital injection, escrow, commercial LC flows, and physical POS settlement must be anchored at a Schedule I bank. A foreign EMI may additionally require FINTRAC registration as a money services business when delivering services to Canadian-resident entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the market standard for initial onboarding of a BC ULC with non-resident shareholders. At least one director or authorized signatory must attend an in-person commercial banking interview at a Canadian branch; remote video verification is accepted only under enhanced due-diligence overrides with notarized corporate documents, a registered BC agent, and a designated commercial account manager. Fully remote account opening is rarely granted for ULCs with offshore beneficial owners and is contingent on the bank's EDD framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant operations flagged for potential cash deposit structuring and VAT/sales under-declaration risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquiring agreement with POS terminal coverage, card-to-cash transaction ratio report, daily cash declaration ledger with deposit manifests, POS-to-accounting reconciliation reports, corporate cash management policy establishing low cash thresholds, employee AML training records, and independently prepared quarterly management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners using an unlimited liability company whose share structure and transfer restrictions obscure ultimate control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Corporate Registry long-form extract, registered and beneficial ownership chart, director and shareholder registers, source-of-wealth documentation with bank statements for all 10%+ owners, tax Notices of Assessment, executed shareholder resolution authorizing the banking mandate, and a detailed business plan covering capex, expansion, and capital deployment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire strings involving condiment imports, franchise royalties, or intercompany payments triggering sanctions screening and trade-based money-laundering detection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HS classification listing (e.g., 2103.90), commercial invoices and packing lists, bills of lading, supplier compliance certificates, sanctions-screening software output, a documented transaction flow map, and proof that counterparties are not subject to measures under the Special Economic Measures Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank positions) from the parent entity to the ULC's CAD capital escrow account at a Vancouver branch of a Schedule I bank. Wire narrative must identify the purpose as 'Equity Contribution — Capital Injection per Shareholder Resolution' to satisfy FINTRAC and the bank's unexplained-wealth assessment. Inbound USD should settle via CHIPS/Fedwire to the bank's USD clearing hub with spot conversion only when treasury policy dictates. Deliverables accompanying the funding instruction include the corporate resolution, subscription agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and, where applicable, the Investment Canada Act notification for establishment of a new Canadian business.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and equipment payments should clear by SWIFT MT103 through correspondent banking; high-value condiment imports from Asia are best structured as commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 or documentary collections. Domestic high-value CAD payments clear through Payments Canada's high-value system (LVTS/Lynx), while low-value modernized settlement traverses the Real-Time Rail (RTR); retail merchant acquiring and POS settlement flows sweep daily into the operating account via automated clearing. USD disbursements clear through each Schedule I bank's U.S. correspondent network (RBC Bank, TD Bank N.A., BMO Harris); CNY-denominated import exposure should settle through a Hong Kong offshore-CNH correspondent rather than onshore CNY rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts (CAD/USD and CAD/CNH) executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on onshore CNY and other restricted currencies covering projected supplier payables, including for the condiment supply chain
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD against shareholder loans or construction financing) for long-dated structural hedging
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures listed on CME for overlay hedging subject to the board-approved treasury policy
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX options (CAD/USD and CAD/CNH) for asymmetric protection on volatility in discretionary dining demand and input-cost swings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report and confirmation of registered office, directors, and share structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (BCBCA s. 187)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-filing fee; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to strike the ULC off the register under BCBCA s. 283, resulting in dissolution and potential director liability for post-dissolution obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including T2S(100), Schedule 1 reconciliation, and financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each fiscal period (ITA s. 150(1)(a))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, repeat failure 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months (ITA s. 162(1)-(2)); daily compound interest under ITA s. 161; loss carry-back rights expire if the return is filed more than 3 years late

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual payroll information return: T4 Slips and T4 Summary for restaurant staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last business day of February following each calendar year (federal due-date rules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 per-day late-filing penalty on the T4 Summary (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); CAD 100 per missing T4 slip up to CAD 7,500 (ITA s. 162(6)-(7)); gross-negligence penalties under ITA s. 163(2) for intentional omissions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Annual Payroll Report and WorkSafeBC annual premium reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: WorkSafeBC (Workers' Compensation Board of British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the employer's fiscal year-end (calendar-year restaurant: by March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-payment penalty on unpaid premiums after 30 days plus daily interest; estimated assessment at the highest premium rate for missing reports; collection, garnishment, and director personal liability under the Workers Compensation Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business licence annual renewal (food-primary restaurant licence)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Host municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar licence year; renewal due by January 31 for Vancouver (municipal schedule varies by city and seating capacity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a municipal late fee, licence suspension, bylaw ticketing, and potential closure order for operating an unlicensed food premise

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: BCBCA contains no revenue-based audit threshold: a private ULC must appoint a statutory auditor only if it is a reporting issuer or if any eligible shareholder refuses a written audit waiver; the audit requirement may otherwise be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution under BCBCA s. 204. In practice, US-parent group consolidation, bank covenants, or gross revenue above CAD 1,000,000 will contractually mandate an independent audit under IFRS or Canadian ASPE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or Canadian ASPE (Part II) for the entity financial statements; the T2 must reconcile accounting income to tax income under ITA ss. 9-12 using Schedule 1; if the ULC has elected US partnership classification, the Canadian statutory books continue to follow Canadian GAAP/ASPE while US tax reporting follows the Form 8832 election.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not require a standalone annual UBO registry return for a private non-reporting ULC. The BC Annual Report confirms the registered office, directors, and share structure, which serves as the registrar's baseline ownership record. Share transfers, new share issuances, and director changes must be recorded in the company's statutory registers within 14 days of the event (BCBCA ss. 45-52, 118); the ULC must pass and file unanimous shareholder resolutions for audit waivers and keep the underlying ownership schedule of ULC shares (which carry unlimited liability) in the central securities register. The registered office and registers remain open for inspection by shareholders and lien-creditors under the BCBCA.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Central securities register (register of members with share-transfer ledgers and ULC share-liability notices)
Register of directors (names, residential and registered addresses, consents to act)
Minute book (records of directors' and shareholders' resolutions, including annual audit-waiver resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 260 - 1,100 per annum (approximately CAD 350 - 1,500) for a Vancouver registered office, corporate agent, and corporate-secretarial maintenance package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 for a single-entity ULC statutory audit by a Canadian CPA firm under IFRS/ASPE; USD 3,000 - 8,000 for a review engagement where the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

stage_6.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Statements (Income Tax Act / Excise Tax Act)
stage_6.triggering_act: Use of POS 'zapper' software or manual records that erase cash sales from hotpot dine-in; sustained under-reporting of gross revenue and input tax credits; failure to report condiment wholesale sales.
stage_6.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under ITA s.239(1): fine of up to 200% of the tax deliberately evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163.2: 50% of understated tax; GST/HST penalties under Excise Tax Act s.280(1.1) plus daily compound interest; CRA may freeze bank accounts and seize assets.
stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly participate in false reporting can be personally charged under s.239; the corporate veil may be pierced for fraudulent misrepresentation; they face civil restitution (CRA can recover from directors), criminal fines, travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years.
